report.summary: Likely wear out in Component - Fan Assembly, Component - Bus Capacitor. Start with the troubleshooting steps below and confirm before replacing parts.

predicted.rationale: 1394 axis modules most often come back with worn bus capacitors and cooling fans; wear-out is the leading cause for this family.

procedure.title: Fan / Cooling - Worn / End of Life
steps: For a Worn/End-of-Life cause code on a fan assembly, check first for elevated bearing noise/vibration and reduced RPM under load: the classic signature of fan-bearing wear.
Verify airflow/RPM against the unit's rated spec. A worn fan often still spins but underperforms before it fully seizes.
Do not attempt to lubricate sealed fan bearings not designed for field relubrication. Replace the fan assembly as a unit once wear is confirmed.

Where available, check the fan's duty-cycle/runtime hours against its rated service life to distinguish premature failure (investigate airflow/temperature root cause) from expected end-of-life wear-out.
After replacement, verify airflow/RPM against spec before closing up the unit.

report.summary: Likely wear out in Motors - Bearings, Motors - Encoder / Resolver. Start with the troubleshooting steps below and confirm before replacing parts.

predicted.rationale: MP-Series servo motor returns are dominated by bearing and encoder wear.

procedure.title: Motors - Worn / End of Life
steps: Check for audible or vibration signs of bearing wear before disassembly.
Measure shaft runout and bearing play against the motor's service-manual tolerance.
If an encoder/resolver is implicated, verify signal integrity and mounting alignment before replacing the sensor itself.
Replace bearings as a matched set, not individually, and re-grease per the motor's lubrication spec.
Re-test running current draw and vibration signature against baseline after reassembly.

report.summary: Likely component failure in PCBA - Other. Start with the troubleshooting steps below and confirm before replacing parts.

predicted.rationale: Component failure on a circuit board is the most common outcome across all product families.

procedure.title: PCBA / Circuitry - Component Failure
steps: Power down and discharge the unit per lockout/tagout procedure before opening the enclosure.
Visually inspect the affected PCBA for obvious component damage: scorching, cracked packages, bulging/leaking electrolytic capacitors, lifted or cold solder joints.
Before re-energizing, check for shorts/continuity issues across primary power rails with a multimeter.
If a specific component is visually suspect, confirm with an in-circuit or out-of-circuit component test before replacing it.
Replace the failed component at the board level by reference designator where feasible, rather than the whole assembly.
Re-run the full functional test sequence against standard acceptance criteria before return to service.
